messages.author: 8bf0927cf6c5a784
messages.subject: Error in contour.default
parts:
I tried running the R part of Sequenza and just trying to replicate the most basic example:
sequenza_extract = sequenza.extract("sample.seqz.gz")
sequenza_fit = sequenza.fit(sequenza_extract)
sequenza.results(sequenza.extract = sequenza_extract, cp.table = sequenza_fit, sample.id = "sample", out.dir="sequenza_results")

Unfortunately, I get an error:
> sequenza.results(sequenza.extract = sequenza_extract, cp.table = sequenza_fit, sample.id = "sample", out.dir="sequenza_results")
Error in contour.default(x = cp.table$ploidy, y = cp.table$cellularity,  :
  invalid NA contour values

Am I doing something wrong?

messages.author: dad6980b76d10753
messages.subject: Re: Error in contour.default
parts:
H Igor,
This problem could occur when one or more segment is really small and produce an NA.
As a easy fix, you can try to use the newer version of the package.
In my opinion is a much better version., there are tons of fixes, and both the model and the segmentation have improved.
You can even use segmentation results from external tools (If you already have the segment called with other software)
Your can install it directly with devtools:

library(devtools)


install_bitbucket(repo = "sequenza", username = "ffavero", ref = "dnorm")


Hopefully this would fix your problem, otherwise you can send me the segmentation from the sequenza.extract object, and I'll try to fix the behaviour of the function.

(I've tested extensively but I might not ahave experienced all the possible problems).

Thanks

Francesco

messages.author: dad6980b76d10753
messages.subject: Re: Error in contour.default
parts:
Hi Igor,

With your data I would try to use different segmentation parameters; for instance in the sequneza.extract command I would try the argument breaks.method = "full".
This uses two segmentations merging the default on heterozygous positions as well a "classical" segmentation on the depth ratio only.
It might lead to smaller segments, but you will gain in precision.

I'm curious, is this targeted re-sequencing? single cell sequencing?

If it's targeted sequencing at hight depth (~500X or 1000X), and you have validated mutations, you could use a different model which included in the package. We didn't test it too much - due to lack of data, mainly-.

You can try in the sequenza.fit the argument method = "mufreq". This would use the mutations frequency instead the segmentations results.

I'm sorry for the vague support I'm giving you here, but the technology you are using have some practical things impeding the full use of the package.
(Of course we should be able to work around it though)

Francesco
